review: 不愧是打越剛太郎

Escape rooms puzzles in the context of a visual novel about strangers trapped in a death game. The story kicker is that only certain combinations of them can progress together through different rooms, and the group tension as they're unsure who to trust in teaming up with.

Highest possible recommendation for anyone interesting in escape rooms. Unless you absolutely cannot stand visual novels, it is a must buy.

One note, that there are two format options for dialog in the first game, 999: Adventure Mode (spoken dialog only) and Novel Mode (narration included). I cannot stress enough on how everyone should only choose Novel Mode. The original Nintendo DS version had a late game story element that is one of the most brilliant reveals that I've ever seen in a video game. Unfortunately, while this version made a lot of quality of life improvements over the original, it did fumble that late game story aspect pretty badly. Playing on Novel Mode at least somewhat helps mitigate the fumble. Beat the True Ending, then look up a video on the final puzzle in the DS version to see how it handled it.

Virtue's Last Reward I would give a 9/10 to compared to the 10/10 for the first game. Puzzles are still great and there is still a compelling story there. It loses a point though for very annoying location transitions (you will curse the map animations) and late game twists that strain credibility (even by magical Nonary standards).

Super good game with probably the best story in any game or movie or show even to ever land on planet earth. Even if you don't like escape rooms I STILL recommend just simply because of how insanely good the story is in these 2 games. Amazing job to the devs, this was a good one.

Watching the same door & movement animations hundreds of times is infuriating, but otherwise, these are excellent visual novels with escape room puzzles mixed in.

[h1]Warning: Spoilers![/h1]
This review contains spoilers for 999, if you have not completed this game to reach the "true ending" and wish not to get spoiled, please keep your cursor carefully located away, as I have them marked accordingly. Of course, you'll still need to play to fully understand these spoilers, these are extremely limited for your benefit.

So, I purchased this solely with the intent to have a PC version of 999. While I could realistically just have continued to use my dumped copy in an emulator, there is one reason why I didn't, the flow system. If you want to reach 100%, which includes getting that true ending, you're going to want to prefer this version for PC, as the original release does not have a way to jump around. I have not touched the original release of VLR in any manner, so I do not know if that applies here either. I quit VLR rather early on and I will get into why later, so this review is primarily focused on 9 Hours, 9 Persons, 9 Doors.

[h3]Story - 999[/h3]
The story is... strange. The premise you are given at the start is rather interesting, you're trapped on a boat, modified to follow the game set forth by an entity known as Zero, but you never really learn why until... {Spoiler territory!]
[spoiler] You are on the path for the "Safe ending", this is mandatory to do before getting the "true ending" btw. It turns out this is a repeat of an experiment 9 years ago. This experiment was focused on "morphogenetic fields" with the Nonary Games acting as a manner to control it. Speak with Clover, she knows more than what she leads on with...[/spoiler]
I ofc do have a few problems with how this story is told of course... {True ending route spoilers included!]
[spoiler] So, while on your path to achieving the final ending, you're going to experience some hell dealing with some unnecessary exposition, meant to drill home *sighs* "Morphogenetic Fields". Sure, 1 or 2 things talking about it is fine, but you're going to be tortured with AT LEAST 6 long story sections just dedicated to experiments and weird (but fake) phoenomena related to the aforementioned concept. The dog one is real though, which is cool. This then is only really actualized with the true ending, and it just felt like a waste. No real mechanical use for it, you solve a puzzle and then the solution is sent to a participant in the previous version.[/spoiler]
{True Ending Spoilers!] [spoiler] Speaking of which, June... She's supposed to have died in the previous Nonary game, but then how was she still alive when completing THIS one? How did she suddenly vanish, then when you magically save her, not just... return?! This just feels like a severe lack of effort for this ending.[/spoiler]
At the very least, Zero is an interesting villain and there's an understandable reason the game happened again, {safe/true ending spoilers] [spoiler] and Ace was actually a pretty neat twist villain, and the breadcrumbs they left for him are rather satisfying.[/spoiler]
Didn't really enjoy the fact that you need to get all 3 "bad" endings before you can get to the ending you want.

[h3]Puzzles - 999[/h3]
The puzzles are okay, at best. There's a calculator, but you never really need to use it through the whole game, which is rather disappointing. I mostly just felt bored when solving each one, no real challenge, like if it was designed for a kid to solve. As an example, the crux of Door 5 AKA [spoiler]the First Class Cabin[/spoiler] is to find objects and then just do trial and error to find the solution. I particularly find these kinds of puzzles to be wasteful of my time since the best puzzles are about thinking through a solution, instead of blindly finding the solution. Sadly, its either guesswork or you immediately find the answer for these puzzles

[h3] Overall - 999 [/h3]
5/10 (meh) - Its got great foundations, but it just never really had much more of a spark. The game might have also benefited from hand-drawn environments instead of pre-rendered ones that clash with the art style of the characters. It survived the transition from DS to PC with minimal losses.

[h2] Virtue's Last Reward [/h2]
This game comes bundled in with 999, so technically it is supposed to be considered a "good deal", but I'm gonna be honest, the game kinda drags itself down so much that I wouldn't really consider paying for VLR if it were sold individually. To get things started, let's look at our villain, Zero 3. Its a rabbit, and he is annoying. Sure, you need a bad guy for these stories, but this bad guy was not threatening from the shadows, but instead just... annoying. I genuinely would have played this game more had the villain been designed to not sound so insufferable. Even disabling auditory dialog and reading everything just made it too unbearable.
I only got so far as completing the Crew Quarters, and after returning from it and seeing 03's ugly mug on my screen again, I just closed the game. Speaking of, the puzzles in the quarters felt a bit more in-depth, although, again, it didn't feel like a challenge, just peg-in-hole type stuff. I would like to know why the boxcutting knife + the aluminum foil gave us answers corresponding to the desks, there's nothing telling Sigma that these shapes are what matters, or how he scored the sheets in a manner where they aren't reflecting, because I noticed a glaring oversight from the art team here, the underside of the sheets don't have holes textured on.

This game doesn't feel like it really translated its presence on 3DS to PC with any sort of tact; in the small amount of time I spent playing, I felt like I was out of place with my inputs. Crafting was very clearly designed for a small touchscreen interface too much, and accessing your inventory in general is a chore. It took me more clicks to solve the initial puzzle than it did to complete most puzzle areas in 999, and it was mostly because of how I have to manually scroll to each item than to just click each item I need to. One look at the Memo screen and I decided that I wasn't ever gonna use it in a legitimate manner. It was clearly a holdover, and any notes you take focused on the background elements won't mean anything. I didn't even bother checking the flow screen, since I knew if I had to deal with 03 another time, I was just gonna drop this game and move on.

[h1] Overall - The full collection [/h1]
If you're getting this thinking its a good deal as a bundle, don't. I honestly wouldn't recommend playing VLR at all. If you want to get this, think of it as just buying 999 and having VLR tacked on. 999 is great as a VN, but not so much as a game, so just pull up a guide and stick to paying attention to the story.

Zero Escape: The Nonary games - це бандл одразу з двох ігор однієї франшизи, 9 Persons 9 Hours 9 Doors(далі - 999) та Virtue's Last Reward(далі - VLR) і даний відгук не містить у собі спойлерів далі перших двох-трьох годин кожної з них, Я загалом раджу якнайменше взаємодіяти з контентом про ці ігри перед тим як ви їх пройдете, оскільки сюжетні повороти та загадки є дуже важливою частиною наративу, ігри задумані таким чином, що ви будете по-інакшому дивитися на одні й ті самі події відповідно того, як багато ви знаєте, і пройти гру вперше ви можете лише один раз, спойлери можуть зіпсувати враження
В обидвох іграх ви - учасник смертельної Нонарної(Дев'яткової) гри, де вам потрібно розгадувати квест-кімнати та досліджувати середовище разом із вісьмома співучасниками аби мати можливість вибратися, чи то всією групою, чи то самотужки. Головною особливістю франшизи є звивиста система шляхів, де кожен ваш вибір впливає на перебіг сюжету і розкриває різних персонажів з найцікавіших сторін, і для розгадування кінцевої загадки вам потрібно буде побачити їх всіх. Але не потрібно лякатися репетативності, даний реліз містить дуже інтуїтивну систему Флоучарту, завдяки якій ви, без усіляких гайдів, можете стрибати по різних шляхах і чітко бачите, чого вам бракує, а функція скіпу дає змогу не перечитувати вже читаний текст. Також виділю дизайн квест кімнат, який, хоча й має як основну функцію розбавити суцільний текст та залучити гравця до процесу, також містить у собі важливі сюжетні відомості та характеризацію персонажів, та й самі загадки загалом цікаво розгадувати до самого кінця
Найбільшою перевагою обох ігор є першокласна робота з перссонажами. На кожному етапі вам доводиться обирати, з якими персонажами та в яку кімнату ви підете, і найцікавіше те, що персонажі є автономними і будуть діяти відповідно до того, яку інформацію в квест кімнатах мають і які предмети отримають. Не довіряєте комусь із персонажів? Йдіть разом з ним/нею разом аби приглядати і дізнатися більше, чи навпаки, тримайтесь осторонь, щоб самим не постраждати від їхніх дій
І головне пам'ятайте, цій історії можна довіряти. Жоден з персонажів не знаходиться в цій смертельній грі просто так, жодна обмовка чи дивна фраза не є випадковістю, жодна механіка не є простою відеоігровою умовністю.

999 - це перша гра франшизи, яка значно коротша за своє продовження (20 годин проти 40, 9 квест-кімнат проти 16) і є самодостатньою. Присутня повна озвучка діалогів англійською та японською, а всі спрайти персонажів виконані в 2д, стилістика красивіша за всі продовження на мою думку, але то таке. Гра містить два режими, режим новели та режим живого діалогу. Це артефакт оригінального походження гри, Нінтендо дс, що має два екрани і на одному з екранів ви бачили світ та діалоги, а на іншому були слова оповідача. Єдина різниця між двома режимами полягає в тому, що новельний режим дає більше реплік оповідача, які дуже важливі для розуміння сюжету, тому причин грати без нього не дуже багато, просто вирізаєте собі контент

VLR - це пряме продовження 999, вона є довшою та головним нововведенням є так звані AB games, після проходження квест-кімнат ви будете грати в Дилему В'язня проти гравців, з якими проходили квест-кімнату, на очки. Гравець, який заробляє 9 очків, може відкрити двері та покинути гру вижившим разом з усіма, хто теж має 9 очків, але вихід можна відкрити лише один раз. Це блискуче нововведення, оскільки воно дає гравцю персональні ставки під час вибору і змушує вас аналізувати характер кожного з гравців та робити оптимальний, особистий вибір, з наслідками якого вам доведеться мати справу, оскільки зрадників ніхто не любить, а занадто добрими люблять користуватися. Ця гра дає персонажам ще більше можливості виражати свої характер та ідеали, а також є каталізатором конфліктів. І хоча за багатьма показниками VLR є кращою, але прямим апгрейдом 999 її не назвати - 3д модельки замість мальованих спрайтів банально виглядають гірше та менш живо, різко збільшується кількість сайфай елементів, через що атмосфера дуже відмінна до першої частини, та й збільшення масштабу історії не всім фанатам до вподоби. Але особисто я полюбив сиквел та його персонажів навіть більше, ніж першу частину, оскільки він розвиває ігроладні ідеї першої частини та ще глибше інтегрує ігровий процес візуальної новели(здавалося б, який ігровий процес у візуальній новелі?) в свій наратив, через що дана історія може існувати виключно як відеогра і вона використовує всі можливості свого медіуму на максимум, чого дуже не вистачає у жанрі

Загалом, я раджу даний бандл усім фанатам детективу, вбивчих ігор та загалом хороших історій з неортодоксальним способом викладу сюжету. Це унікальні та дуже недооцінені ігри, які точно не залишать вас байдужими

999 довольно сильно пострадала из-за портирования. Оригинальная игра была разработана для консолей с двумя экранами, и по полной это использовала. Из-за этого, при переносе на ПК в геймплейном и повествовательном плане пришлось сделать некоторые изменения, многие из которых похерили повествование. Все еще отличная история, с неожиданными твистами и неплохими головоломками.

VLR - одна из лучших игр, в которые я играл. Головоломки стали продуманнее и интереснее, персонажи круче, чем в первой части (тут уже субъективщина, но Фай и Луна навсегда в сердечке), наверное самая крутая реализация получения разных концовок, что я когда-либо видел, ну и грамотное повествование, когда ты до последнего нихера не понимаешь, пока все не складывается воедино. Единственный минус второй части - кривые 3д модельки и долгие анимации передвижения по комнатам, что быстро надоедает. В остальном же, всем советую, правда. Оно того стоит.

SOBRE = Nine Hours, Nine Persons, Nine Doors

Faz bastante tempo que eu não jogo alguma VN e eu não lembro de ter jogado nenhum jogo de puzzle por vontade própria na vida. Então "Zero Escape: Nine Hours, Nine Persons, Nine Doors" tinha uma missão bem difícil para conseguir me entreter. Ou pelo menos era isso que eu achava. Logo de cara o jogo mortal, os personagens esquisitos e mistério me fizeram ficar fissurado na história para descobrir o que diabos estava acontecendo. 

Os puzzles aqui acontecem em formato de "escape rooms" onde nós, o jogador no papel de Junpei e outros 8 participantes, buscamos por maneiras de escapar, obviamente, e conseguir assim seguir caminho pelos ambientes mortais em busca da porta 9 que é a saída desse jogo sádico. Eu ADOREI praticamente todas as escape rooms do jogo. Nem muito difíceis, nem muito fáceis. Quase sempre você encontra alguma bizarrice ou algum puzzle criativo pra fazer.

Mesmo tendo o "point n click" como mecânica padrão para a procura de pistas e solução dos puzzles nas escape rooms, eu nenhum momento eu me vi preso em algum dos desafios por não ter clicado em algum lugar mega especifico ou por não saber aonde deveria clicar, o que poderia facilmente acontecer já que os cenários são todos em 3D (na verdade, tá mais pra prints de cenários 3D). Ótimo trabalho em fazer os cenários serem facilmente lidos e interpretados pelo jogador.  

Algumas das rotas não canônicas do jogo me pareceram meio jogadas ou pouco lógicas quando você descobre todo o mistério e o pq das coisas terem acontecido durante o final verdadeiro do jogo, mas já que essas rotas não são canônicas, eu acho que dá pra ignorar. Outra questão é que alguns personagens que se mostram importantes no fim ou durante a história não conseguem ser tão carismáticos assim como deveriam. Não acho nenhum ruim, longe disso, mas acho que daria para dar uma caprichada nessa parte em alguns deles. 

Aproveitando que eu falei das rotas, a história desse jogo é uma maluquice tremenda e eu não esperava nem um pouco que o final fosse tão esquisito. Estava pensando que seria algo mais pé no chão e terminei voando.

Vi que algumas pessoas reclamaram sobre o jogo ficar reforçando bastante nas dicas durante puzzles (Não reparei nisso. Só nas vezes em que você pode ficar insistindo em clicar no mesmo lugar várias vezes e então o jogo entende que vc está perdidinho e tenta ajudar) e ficar te relembrando várias vezes sobre acontecimentos durante a história (o que ajuda bastante já que são várias rotas diferentes, salas, símbolos e informações diferentes em rotas específicas), mas não vi isso como algo negativo e até acho que isso é bem comum em VNs? Não tenho certeza, mas essas questões não me surpreenderam ou incomodaram. Recomendo bastante o jogo. 

SOBRE = Virtue's Last Reward

Sendo sincero, eu comecei "Virtue's Last Reward" pensando que teria uma experiência esquisita assim como no primeiro, mas que não iria conseguir se equiparar ao antecessor e acabaria sendo apenas uma outra boa Visual Novel.
Cara... Se o jogo anterior chutou o balde com a sua história esquisita, mistérios, puzzles e maluquices, esse segundo jogo chutou o balde, pisou, jogou pra cima, fez embaixadinhas e terminou com um gol de placa. QUE MALUQUICE FOI ESSA?
Claro que algumas coisas não são tão bem explicadas, outras não fazem muito sentido e apesar de algumas perguntas serem respondidas outras são criadas e não respondidas no processo. Então isso ajuda a criar o clima de mistério e dúvidas. Mas se for analisar, no primeiro jogo acontecer a mesma coisa KKKK

Eu nem consigo falar muito sobre a história já que ela consegue ser tão viajada e complexa que mesmo quem "entende" tem dificuldade de explicar de maneira apropriada. Só sei que eu curti bastante, tiveram bem mais momentos "WTF" do que no primeiro e apesar de algumas revelações serem até meio obvias de se perceber, o jogo ainda consegue te enganar até o momento da revelação. Estava tudo na frente do seu nariz o tempo todo e você não percebeu.  Claro que algumas delas só funcionam pq o jogo te esconde alguma informação até o ultimo minuto, pq algum personagem é super misterioso, pq frases são ditas pela metade ou pq algum personagem "esqueceu" de expor alguma informação importante. Mas apesar dessas questões ainda são revelações interessantes que criam momentos bem memoráveis. 

Ainda acho que prefiro os personagens do "Nine Hours, Nine Persons, Nine Doors" pensando no elenco como um todo, mas os desse jogo também são bem interessantes e cumprem bem os seus papeis (Tirando um ou outro que não servem pra muita coisa). Já sinto saudades deles. Os finais de cada personagem, em sua maioria, são muito mais bem pensados e elaborados que no jogo antecessor fazendo com que cada um consiga trazer alguma informação, revelação, pergunta ou maluquice nova. 

Porém algo que não é tão positivo assim é a repetição que esse jogo carrega durante a gameplay. Você vai voltar MUITAS vezes pro "começo" da história para tentar uma outra rota já que para conseguir os finais é necessário ter conhecimento de informações especificas sobre eventos na história. O jogo te trava e só depois de descobrir a informação para liberar a rota x,y ou z que você poderá progredir pela caminho especifico. Ao todo são 10 caminhos "Locked" ao longo da várias rotas e bifurcações diferentes e dependendo da ordem de rotas que você escolher, provavelmente terá que chegar perto do final do jogo pra conseguir começar a libera-las.
Sim, o jogo te da a opção de pular os diálogos repetidos, mas nem sempre é fácil de decorar em que momento o dialogo repetido acaba e o novo começa (já que isso acontece em momentos diferentes da história) e sempre da aquele medo de "será que eu perdi alguma informação?", "Será que teve um dialogo diferente e eu não vi?". No primeiro jogo, por ser uma história mais simples (o que é bizarro de se dizer KKKKK), eu basicamente não tive que ler ou pular quase nenhum dialogo repetido, mas nesse segundo jogo acontece bastante.

Vale também citar que pelo fato do jogo ser 100% 3D agora fez com que ele ficasse mais lento em relação ao primeiro. Ter que ir de um lado pro outro de uma sala grande usando as setas do teclado é bem chato e piora ainda mais quando você está perdido em alguma parte da escape room e fica indo de um lado pro outro do mapa em câmera lenta pra ver se deixou alguma informação para trás. ISSO SEM CONTAR OS MOMENTOS INTERMINAVEIS DE ANDAR PELO MAPA DA INSTALAÇÃO E VER ANIMAÇÕES DE PORTAS ABRINDO E FECHANDO.

Falando em puzzles, eles são mais difíceis nesse jogo aqui. O primeiro jogo é super tranquilo de terminar sem precisar de algum guia ou dicas, mas nesse segundo jogo eles deram uma caprichada. Ou pelo menos os primeiros puzzles parecem ser mais difíceis. Depois você se acostuma. Agora você tem a opção de resolve-los do modo padrão "Hard" ou mudar para uma versão mais fácil "Easy". Mas claro que você só consegue o final verdadeiro se passar por todas as escape rooms no "Hard". Tirando alguns pouco intuitivos ou algumas partes de quebrar a cabeça, eu adorei os desse jogo também. 

Os diálogos são repetitivos e redundantes em algumas momentos, mas se você jogou o primeiro não vai se incomodar tanto com isso durante a jogatina. No fim "Zero Escape: Virtue's Last Reward" é um Visual Novel MUITO legal, com uma história que te deixa maluquinho, revelações bombásticas e personagens carismáticos. Recomendo bastante :D

Zero Escape: The Nonary Games is a 2 in 1 bundle that includes the first two games in the Zero Escape trilogy. For those who know nothing about this franchise, it’s essentially a mystery visual novel series where escape rooms are the main interactive feature. It’s just as much a puzzle game as it is story based (both of which are extremely confusing at times). I constantly had a pen and paper next to me while playing and I don’t regret it, these games make you THINK. 

Without spoiling anything, I think it’s important to make clear that all Zero Escape games feature multiple endings. Do NOT stop playing once you hit your first game over. These games require you to play through multiple endings to access more of the story. It’s a unique design choice but these stories don’t work otherwise. 

The first game in this bundle, 999, is a remake of the original DS port with brilliant voice acting and 2D visuals. It’s largely considered the best game in the trilogy (though personally I prefer VLR). The only negative point I have with this game is that it can force you to replay through escape rooms you already cleared when searching for certain endings. Thankfully this is something the sequel fixes entirely, and 999 isn’t a terribly long game so it’s not a huge deal. 

The sequel, Virtues Last Reward is around twice the length of 999 and has a completely different appearance with 3D models and new atmosphere. It can be quite jarring at first and honestly, I really didn’t like VLR in the beginning. There was a bit too much change, I didn’t care for the story, and it felt like I was just hitting pointless endings constantly that meant nothing (spoiler: they weren’t pointless). It was only after about 15 hours I really started to care about the game at all. By the time I finished the game though I loved it more than 999 and it was so unlike anything I’d ever played. It’s definitely a slowburn but I’m so grateful for the experience. 

It’s hard to compare this franchise to any other game because of how original it is. If you’re not opposed to a fascinating story game that will make you rack your brain trying to solve a problem, I definitely recommend giving Zero Escape a shot. I can guarantee it will surprise you.

Что ж... я прошел 1 (999) и 2 (VLR) игры после знакомства с Zero Time Dilemma. Сейчас даже удивлён почему я слышал так много негатива к третьей части, хотя у неё больше положительного, чем попадалось ранее в мое инфополе.

Сейчас я не вижу большого смысла для себя подробно описывать игры. Сюжет прикольный, только много в VLR накрутили с идейными... условно, "перестановками". Сами повороты были классными, даже 1 ключевой из концовки предугадал в середине игры чисто из особенностей игровой условности (классно, что в Zero Time Dilemma есть такое же и осознал это только сейчас). Визуал, конечно, у второй и третьей игры такой себе: вторая не смогла в модельки, третья в анимации (но терпимо). 

Геймплейно мне понравилась... каждая часть по-разному. Первая часть интуитивно понятна в головоломках и внутриигровой калькулятор не нужен. Вторая самая **** по части головоломок... душиться можно с начала и особенно с середины до концовки всей игры. Третья же излишне упрощена. Как бы геймплей даже стыкуется с контекстом каждой игры, но вот не хватило в двух частях правильного баланса. Однако...

Как же хочется похейтить VLR за функцию пропуска. Без нее никак: повторения в разных рутах прокликивать скучно, их много, поэтому пропуск должен помочь. Но проблема кроется в ляпе относительно всего жанра: привычно для визуальных новелл давать функцию пропуска уже прочитанного ранее текста, но тут ты пропускаешь любой текст, поэтому велик риск пропустить что-то важное в другом руте при одинаковом начале. Да и как же бесила куча анимаций открывающихся и закрывающихся дверей + беготня по карте. Толку от всех этих анимаций, если только в редких случаях необходимы объяснения по поводу перемещений героев (в 999 с этим нормально, там карту показали, убрали и забыли, но не в VLR). Мдэ, зачем так надо было?

В оставшемся: музыка классная, парадоксы интересные (китайская комната интересная, но пояснять за кота Шредингера кучу времени - может это у японцев не так известно), персонажи по-своему интересные в каждой части (Clover - разочарование что в 999, что в VLR). Самое ценное во всех играх - теории про работу сознания человека и детали, которые доступны к восприятию игрока, просто нужно быть подозрительнее и искать их хорошенько.

I really enjoyed both 999 and VLR (the two games included in The Nonary Games). In fact, I'd say they are some of my favourite games of all time, particularly in terms of story, though the escape rooms were fun too. 

I don't usually like Visual Novels, as many of them feel the same or are just reading with hardly any gameplay, but these games do not have that problem. The rooms and puzzles were almost always quite fun, I found the dialogue and characters to be interesting (and I will forever remember what Prosopagnosia is) and the overall story to be quite robust (particularly with 999) 

VLR was interesting but also gigantic. There were so many paths and certain ones felt very confusing at times. However, my mind was quite blown by the ending and it put a lot of pieces together in a very clever way that had gone very over my head. I went into it thinking it wasn't going to make any sense, and came out feeling shocked at how well everything fit in the end (As Phi would undoubtedly say: "Isn't it obvious???"), even if some of it was a bit bloated I think it was well worth it. 

I wish I could play these games all over again for the first time, as they have really interesting and cool mechanics, meshed with a great story and fun point-and-click escape room puzzles. I do NOT recommend buying the "Zero Escape Trilogy Bundle" though, as I feel the second half of the third game really hurt my interest in the series, but these two games in one package of The Nonary Games are a beautiful combo together. 

Highly recommend buying this game! It's are VERY worth the price in my opinion, and I wish more people were aware 999 and VLR existed!

100%'d 999, got six hours into VLR before deciding to take a very long break

TL;DR: 999 is great. VLR will irritate the ♥♥♥♥ out of you, and it's the majority of this port on Steam.

999 is great. I don't have much problems with it. The puzzles are great for what they are, the characters are decent, and the story has some nice twists into it.

The problem is VLR. There's also so many little things that just irritate the hell out of me, mainly being the constant door opening animations and the dot on the map sequences that play ANY time Sigma goes anywhere in the map, including places he's been before. Any other VN? Instantly skip time to when Sigma reaches the location. This VN? Here, have an UNSKIPPABLE CUTSCENE of a dot going through the entire map, playing every single door and elevator animation it can.

I also have massive problems with one of the characters because of their relation to the previous game. IYKYK. They got massively character assassinated, and since I played VLR right after finishing 999 I think I probably got more whiplash than most.

Character models also look worse than 999, mostly because of the transition from 2D animated sprites to 3D models. The above character's model is the one in particular that I have a lot of problems with since it just has a permanent smile attached onto it, even when they are screaming about another character who just died.

The story lock system here also just kinda sucks? With 999, the reason for the locks was because they blocked off the big storylines, so that the player knew what would specifically get them further in the story. In VLR, they just have so many locks for no good reasons for storylines that clearly end right then and there. This kinda forces you to bounce around timelines, and by the time you find the key to the lock you will almost certainly have forgotten what actually happened in that specific storyline.

I also think that the story tree was poorly implemented here. There is ZERO indication which order you should be playing these in, but if you go to any guide the author will probably give you an order of which branches to go to first. The reason for this is that some plotlines casually talk about significant spoilers from other endings that you have zero reason to know now. In my case, my first choice was the right branch (Alice). I first picked Trust, which was a normal storyline all things considered up until the story lock. Then I picked Betray, which proceeded to dump a completely game-changing story revelation that the game apparently considered at that point to be known information, with how casually it revealed it. There was ZERO indication of that reveal in the Trust storyline up until the lock, nor in the pre-first choice story. Once again, there was zero indication that I should be saving this ending for last as well. :/

I also thought the writing felt very mediocre, but take with a grain of salt: 999's story was decent all things considered and I was only 30%, maybe 35% into VLR when I decided to take a long hiatus. I also didn't like any of the characters, definitely not nearly as much as 999 (which is especially bad because one of these characters has a direct connection to 999), but once again take it with a grain of salt.

The puzzles are fine. I don't really enjoy this pure style of puzzle in games (I like investigation puzzles like Obra Dinn and Golden Idol), but 999's story kept me playing through them. VLR felt the same, so if you're playing this game for the puzzles (for some reason) I guess you'll enjoy them? I think the safe code system (one code for escape, one code for optional bonus content/achievement) is kinda lazy though.

I left a negative review because the bulk of this game on Steam is VLR. 999 will take you roughly about 12 hours to play through with 6 endings. VLR has 28 endings, and a good number of them are as long as the true ending of 999. 999 is good, but it's only the minority of this port on Steam.

First of all, don't play this expecting it to be a deathgame, like Danganronpa. A couple of characters will die, but it's not the same experience, thanks to the choices and the flowchart you'll keep going back lots of times. Zero Escape is more about the mystery surrounding all these characters, the place you're all trapped in and the events happening thorugh the game. To solve this mystery and to escape, the characters have to solve various escaperoom-like puzzles.

Both games were amazing, and even if they felt a little slow at times (specially VLR), once you reach a point where you start getting more information, you just won't be able to stop until finishing the game. The plot twists are mind-blowing, in 999, at least, even if a little complicated or difficult to believe in some cases (looking at VLR). Characters are also amazing, but not without some japanese fan service and unfunny humour. Nothing that will keep you from enjoying the experience, but there are some scenes sure to make you sigh. My favourites are probably Clover, K, Dio and Phi.

Oh, yeah, also important to say: PLAY 999 IN NOVEL MODE. I know action mode's more cool and easier to read, but there's a plot twist that will make much more sense if you play in novel mode. (I've read the DS version is the best one to play, but it doesn't allow to travel through the flowchart like you'll be able to do in this one. In my opinion, it's way cheaper and easier to play this the whole trilogy in Steam, even if some things in 999 will be a little bit worse, it will still be an amazing game).

그치만 1편 쪽이 더 인간들이 서로 공격적인 분위기라 재밌었던 것 같긴 함...
2편은 너무 진행이 고구마임... 보통은 배신 누른 놈들 일단 집단 린치부터할 것 같은데...
(저는 이래서 엔딩까지도 [spoiler]집단 최면이나 전원 재현 로봇[/spoiler] 같은 걸 의심하기까지 했습니다.)


저는 이 게임을 우연히도 더욱 작품 주제에 맞게 멋지게도 즐겨버리게 되었는데, 제가 1편 했었을 당시엔 (이 두 편 묶음 중) 1편만 한글 패치가 있고 2편은 없어서 그냥 넘겨버렸었거든요.
그러다 1편 트릭이 2편보다 더 복잡한 이유도 있고 해서 세부 사항을 다 까먹어버렸슴미다...

그런 연유로 오랜 시간이 지나 2편 플레이하며 깔렸던 복선들을 하나도 눈치채지 못하고 있다가, 떡밥을 모두 회수하는 총집편에서 우연히 [spoiler]"과거의 나"[/spoiler]의 지식이 "날아와"버리는 바람에 주인공과 유사한 체험을 해버렸지 뭐에요. 
이야~, 게임은 역시 묵혀놓고 볼 일이에요.

언젠가 누군가 자신이 본 반전 중 가장 좋았다고 보여준 짤이 있었는데, 그게 이 게임이란 점을 알게 된 그 순간에도 과거가 날아들어온 듯한 느낌.
[I]"어???? 어어? 반전 뭐냐? 어라, 근데 이거 본 적 있는 듯한데??"[/I]
